city.name: Shibuya & Shinjuku
city.description: Sangenjaya to Shibuya, Shinjuku and Yotsuya from open data, lit by the real sun: Project PLATEAU's surveyed heights, the Shibuya scramble, the Suga Shrine stairs of Your Name, and the streets Persona 5 drew.

tour.title: Sangenjaya to Shinjuku, from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings. {share:plateau}% of the footprint area stands at a height that Project PLATEAU surveyed, on GSI's laser-scanned bare earth under GSI aerial photographs.

tour.title: The scramble
tour.text: Four streets meet at Shibuya's scramble, and when the lights change every crossing goes green at once, the diagonal too. The white bars are drawn from OpenStreetMap's crosswalks. Hachiko sits on his granite to the south.

tour.title: SHIBUYA SKY, 229 m
tour.text: On Scramble Square's roof (2019): about 2,500 m² of open deck at {landmark:shibuya_sky.deck_m} m, glass at the edge, GEO COMPASS in the middle and the escalator coming up out of the 46th floor.

tour.title: The stairs of Suga Shrine
tour.text: {landmark:suga.otokozaka.steps} stone steps, three and a half metres wide, red iron handrails both sides and down the middle: the 男坂 of Suga Shrine, the stairs of Your Name. The film turns ten this year.

tour.title: Sangenjaya's triangle
tour.text: Between Setagaya-dori and Route 246, the backstreets of Sangenjaya: a bathhouse, a snack bar, a meat shop open all night. A game drew its home town here and called it Yongen-Jaya.

tour.title: Kabukicho after dark
tour.text: Kabukicho Ichibangai's red arch has lit the way in since 1969. The district is named for a kabuki theatre planned after the war that was never built.

tour.title: Where the heights come from
tour.text: Blue: a surveyed height (PLATEAU or OpenStreetMap). Orange: a floor count. Green: an estimate from the neighbours. Towers finished since PLATEAU's survey, such as the Tokyu Kabukicho Tower, keep OpenStreetMap's height.

protection.title: No sun-access rule for public places
protection.summary: Tokyo protects no park's sunlight. The windows are a lunch-hour thought experiment for this project, as in the Marunouchi model.
protection.source_note: Windows are our own choice (noon to 13:00, all year), not law. The Building Standards Act's shadow rule (日影規制, art. 56-2) limits hours of shadow on neighbouring land in residential-type zones; it does not cover public places and does not apply in commercial districts such as Shibuya or Shinjuku.
protection.reading_note: Tokyo keeps standard time all year. Miyashita Park is a roof garden on a mall (2020): its sun here is read at the ground, so treat it with care.
protection.tip: Tip: try a tower on the block south of Yoyogi Park, or beside Shinjuku Gyoen's west gate.

light_show.name: CROSSING LIGHT
light_show.note: SHIBUYA SKY's 18 searchlights on the roof light after sunset with the seasons (Wikipedia). Their times and movement here are illustrative.

shore.encoding: r: 128 + 2 x signed distance to the shoreline (m, water positive); g: sand; b: rock

trees.note: Species are not mapped. Elms stand for the zelkovas (keyaki) of Omotesando and the shrine groves, plane trees for the street planes and ginkgos of Aoyama and Meiji Jingu Gaien. A guess, not a survey.

suga.sources: 男坂: Tokyo stairs database 0008 (52 steps, 3.6 m, 16 m, 27 degrees, two landings, red iron handrails); lines and footprints: OpenStreetMap via Overture; hall ridge: PLATEAU

signs.note: shop signs on street fronts in the districts; indicative, not the real shops' signs

sources.heights: MLIT Project PLATEAU Tokyo 23 wards LOD2 building models (CC BY 4.0), as vector tiles by indigo-lab (MIT)

sources.terrain: GSI Fundamental Geospatial Data DEM5A, 5 m airborne laser survey bare earth (GSI terms of use); 10 m DEM where 5A is absent
sources.imagery: Geospatial Information Authority of Japan (GSI) seamless aerial photographs (GSI terms of use, source attribution)
sources.places: Overture base land use (OpenStreetMap, ODbL); rules: No sun-access rule for public places
sources.trees: Overture base land, tree points and rows (OpenStreetMap, ODbL); heights not mapped
sources.landmarks: Suga Shrine's 男坂 from the Tokyo stairs database (52 steps, 3.6 m, 16 m, 27°, red iron handrails); its hall, torii and furniture placed from OpenStreetMap and photographs; SHIBUYA SKY from SHIBUYA SKY and Wikipedia (229 m, 2,500 m², 18 searchlights, 360 m/min lifts); the Docomo tower's clock (15 m, 150 m up; Tokyo tourism, TV Tokyo) and mast (272 m; SkyscraperPage); Kabukicho's arch (1969; Sanshin Shoji). Signs, screens and shop fronts are indicative.

accuracy.method: that carry both a PLATEAU height and a height tag in OpenStreetMap (an independent source), 20 m and taller
